requirement: Colorado English Learner Professional Development (ELPD) License Renewal Requirement
timing_notes: Beginning September 1, 2025, Colorado now requires teachers renewing their licenses in elementary, English language arts, math, science, social studies, or middle-level subject areas to complete training in Culturally and Linguistically Diverse education ([csi.state.co.us](https://csi.state.co.us/update/january2025update#:~:text=,us%20for%20questions)). This rule, set by the State Board of Education, amounts to 45 clock hours (or equivalent coursework) of English Learner Professional Development for those educators ([staff.tsd.org](https://staff.tsd.org/pd/license-renewal/english-learner-el-designation#:~:text=In%20order%20to%20meet%20the,new%20English%20Learner%20PD%20requirement)) ([staff.tsd.org](https://staff.tsd.org/pd/license-renewal/english-learner-el-designation#:~:text=State%20Board%20of%20Education%20adopted,PD)). Teachers who already hold a CLDE (Culturally & Linguistically Diverse Education) endorsement or have an ELPD designation are considered to have met the requirement. The deadline is tied to individual licensure renewal dates, but effectively all affected teachers statewide must fulfill the EL PD hours or risk being unable to renew their teaching licenses. Failure to comply means a teacher cannot continue teaching in Colorado public schools until the requirement is met.

requirement: Structured English Immersion (SEI) Endorsement Mandate for Teachers
timing_notes: Arizona requires every teacher who instructs English Learners to hold an SEI, ESL, or Bilingual endorsement ([www.azed.gov](https://www.azed.gov/oelas/sei-endorsement#:~:text=All%20Public%20School%20teachers%20working,L)). Practically, most teachers obtain the SEI endorsement by completing 45 hours of approved professional development on teaching ELLs (or equivalent coursework) ([www.law.cornell.edu](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/arizona/Ariz-Admin-Code-SS-R7-2-615#:~:text=b,756.09%28B)). New teachers have up to three years on a provisional SEI endorsement (15-hour training) to complete the full requirements. This is a statewide compliance mandate to ensure teachers are qualified in ELL methodologies.

State law (22 Pa. Code §4.26) mandates that any teacher providing ESL instruction hold an ESL Program Specialist certificate ([www.pa.gov](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/education/programs-and-services/educators/certification/help/certification-faqs/english-as-a-second-language#:~:text=What%20are%20the%20requirements%20to,staff%20ESL%20teaching%20positions)). Districts are responsible for staffing their Language Instruction Educational Programs with properly certified ESL teachers or getting current staff endorsed.
